overall_notes: Pair 3 (Many-to-One Bar Graphs) clears the strict bar with all six categories at Level 4. ALIGNMENT: D1.3 byte-identical, every success criterion ('pick scale', 'read scaled bars', 'build scaled bars') has a named lesson activity and a matching worksheet part; expanded_walkthrough rationale explicitly bridges to Day 2 (frequency tables) and Day 4 (mean/mode). PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH: scale-blind trap is cited to Friel, Curcio & Bright (2001) graph-comprehension hierarchy at intermediate level, and recovery_moves branches three ways by diagnostic (A height-literal, B wrong multiply, C cannot construct). INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE: puppets explicitly optional with voice/stuffed-animal/picture substitutes; movement-learners differentiation provides a body-becomes-bar-graph no-paper path; 12/25/13 = 50 min is realistic for Grade 3. CLARITY_VOICE: Detective Dot anchors hook, action step 6, and consolidation; refrain 'CHECK the scale, MULTIPLY the height — that's the COUNT!' chanted 3x at exit; all success_criteria use 'I can'. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY: INVENT-AND-COMPARE step 6 has pairs design two different scales (1=5 vs 1=10) for the same 50-student data and compare readability — children invent and refine strategies; research citation present. LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY: worksheet Part 3 transfers to counts in the hundreds (100, 200, 300, 400 with scale=100), a justified generalisation beyond the lesson's 50-student practice. Solid pair — pipeline can advance.
